nodes.text: Come in — mind the drying herbs. Sagewort on the left, moonbell on the right, and the smell in the middle is a tincture that is *supposed* to do that. Probably. Almost certainly.

choices.text: How did you come to Amberford?
Any advice for the road north?

nodes.text: Sagewort, moonbell, any honest herb you pull from the verges — coin on the counter, no questions. Half this town's health walks in through that door in a forager's pocket. More than half, actually. I've counted.

Down the High Road, twelve years back — eleven and a half, strictly — with one book and a moonbell cutting wrapped in a stocking. Where from? _Further than the road goes._ The cutting took to the soil here. So did I. That's the whole answer you'll get, and it's more than most.

Carry more tinctures than you think you need, and drink them *earlier* than you think you should — people die holding a full bottle. Pride is the one wound I can't brew for. And past the Last Lamp, walk mornings. Everything old up there sleeps late.
Brewing formulas and the enchanter's treatises — folios on the shelf. The knowledge keeps. See that you do the same.
